passages.text: “At that time,” declares the LORD, “the bones of the kings of Judah, the bones of the officials, the bones of the priests, the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the people of Jerusalem will be removed from their graves.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
He says this will happen at that time.
People will remove the bones of the kings of Judah from their graves.
They will remove the bones of the officials from their graves.
They will remove the bones of the priests from their graves.
They will remove the bones of the prophets from their graves.
They will remove the bones of the people of Jerusalem from their graves.
passages.original: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֣יא נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֡ה וְיֹצִיאוּ אֶת־ עַצְמ֣וֹת מַלְכֵֽי־ יְהוּדָ֣ה וְאֶת־ עַצְמוֹת־ שָׂרָיו֩ וְאֶת־ עַצְמ֨וֹת הַכֹּהֲנִ֜ים וְאֵ֣ת׀ עַצְמ֣וֹת הַנְּבִיאִ֗ים וְאֵ֛ת עַצְמ֥וֹת יוֹשְׁבֵֽי־ יְרוּשָׁלִָ֖ם מִקִּבְרֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: They will be exposed to the sun and moon, and to all the host of heaven which they have loved, served, followed, consulted, and worshiped. Their bones will not be gathered up or buried, but will become like dung lying on the ground.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about the people of Jerusalem and Judah.
Their bones will be taken out of their graves.
People will spread their bones out before the sun.
People will spread their bones out before the moon.
People will spread their bones out before all the stars and heavenly bodies.
These people loved the sun, moon, and stars.
They served the sun, moon, and stars.
They followed the sun, moon, and stars.
They consulted the sun, moon, and stars.
They worshiped the sun, moon, and stars.
No one will gather their bones.
No one will bury their bones.
Their bones will lie on the ground like dung.
passages.original: וּשְׁטָחוּם֩ לַשֶּׁ֨מֶשׁ וְלַיָּרֵ֜חַ וּלְכֹ֣ל׀ צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֗יִם אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֲהֵב֜וּם וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר עֲבָדוּם֙ וַֽאֲשֶׁר֙ הָלְכ֣וּ אַֽחֲרֵיהֶ֔ם וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר דְּרָשׁ֔וּם וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר הִֽשְׁתַּחֲו֖וּ לָהֶ֑ם לֹ֤א יֵאָֽסְפוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א יִקָּבֵ֔רוּ לְדֹ֛מֶן עַל־ פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָ֖ה יִֽהְיֽוּ׃

passages.text: And wherever I have banished them, the remnant of this evil family will choose death over life,” declares the LORD of Hosts.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
He has banished the people.
A remnant from this evil family remains.
They live in many places where the LORD has sent them.
These people choose death instead of life.
passages.original: וְנִבְחַ֥ר מָ֙וֶת֙ מֵֽחַיִּ֔ים לְכֹ֗ל הַשְּׁאֵרִית֙ הַנִּשְׁאָרִ֔ים מִן־ הַמִּשְׁפָּחָ֥ה הָֽרָעָ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את בְּכָל־ הַמְּקֹמ֤וֹת הַנִּשְׁאָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִדַּחְתִּ֣ים שָׁ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃ס

passages.text: So you are to tell them this is what the LORD says: “Do men fall and not get up again? Does one turn away and not return?
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the people of Jerusalem.
He asks a question.
He says, "Do people fall and not get up again?"
He says, "If someone turns away, do they not return?"
passages.original: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הֲיִפְּל֖וּ וְלֹ֣א יָק֑וּמוּ אִם־ יָשׁ֖וּב וְלֹ֥א יָשֽׁוּב׃

passages.text: Why then have these people turned away? Why does Jerusalem always turn away? They cling to deceit; they refuse to return.
passages.sermon:
The people of Jerusalem have turned away from God.
They keep turning away again and again.
They hold tightly to lies.
They refuse to come back to God.
passages.original: מַדּ֨וּעַ שׁוֹבְבָ֜ה הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֛ה יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם מְשֻׁבָ֣ה נִצַּ֑חַת הֶחֱזִ֙יקוּ֙ בַּתַּרְמִ֔ית מֵאֲנ֖וּ לָשֽׁוּב׃

passages.text: I have listened and heard; they do not speak what is right. No one repents of his wickedness, asking, ‘What have I done?’ Everyone has pursued his own course like a horse charging into battle.
passages.sermon:
God is speaking about the people of Jerusalem.
God says, "I have listened."
God says, "I have heard what they say."
They do not speak what is right.
No one repents of his wickedness.
No one asks, 'What have I done?'
Everyone follows his own path.
Each person rushes ahead.
They act like a horse charging into battle.
passages.original: הִקְשַׁ֤בְתִּי וָֽאֶשְׁמָע֙ לוֹא־ כֵ֣ן יְדַבֵּ֔רוּ אֵ֣ין אִ֗ישׁ נִחָם֙ עַל־ רָ֣עָת֔וֹ לֵאמֹ֖ר מֶ֣ה עָשִׂ֑יתִי כֻּלֹּ֗ה שָׁ֚ב בִּמְרֻצוֹתָם כְּס֥וּס שׁוֹטֵ֖ף בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

passages.text: Even the stork in the sky knows her appointed seasons. The turtledove, the swift, and the thrush keep their time of migration, but My people do not know the requirements of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The stork flies in the sky.
The stork knows her appointed seasons.
The turtledove knows her time to come.
The swift knows its time to come.
The thrush knows its time to come.
These birds keep their times of migration.
But My people do not know the requirements of the LORD.
My people do not understand what the LORD asks of them.
passages.original: גַּם־ חֲסִידָ֣ה בַשָּׁמַ֗יִם יָֽדְעָה֙ מֽוֹעֲדֶ֔יהָ וְתֹ֤ר וְסוּס וְעָג֔וּר שָׁמְר֖וּ אֶת־ עֵ֣ת בֹּאָ֑נָה וְעַמִּ֕י לֹ֣א יָֽדְע֔וּ אֵ֖ת מִשְׁפַּ֥ט יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: How can you say, ‘We are wise, and the Law of the LORD is with us,’ when in fact the lying pen of the scribes has produced a deception?
passages.sermon:
The people claim to be wise.
They say, "We have the Law of the LORD."
They believe God's teaching is with them.
But the scribes have written lies.
Their pen has produced deception.
Their wisdom is false.
passages.original: אֵיכָ֤ה תֹֽאמְרוּ֙ חֲכָמִ֣ים אֲנַ֔חְנוּ וְתוֹרַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה אִתָּ֑נוּ אָכֵן֙ הִנֵּ֣ה לַשֶּׁ֣קֶר עָשָׂ֔ה עֵ֖ט שֶׁ֥קֶר סֹפְרִֽים׃

passages.text: The wise will be put to shame; they will be dismayed and trapped. Since they have rejected the word of the LORD, what wisdom do they really have?
passages.sermon:
The wise people will feel shame.
They will become afraid.
They will be caught in a trap.
They have rejected the word of the LORD.
They do not have true wisdom.
passages.original: הֹבִ֣ישׁוּ חֲכָמִ֔ים חַ֖תּוּ וַיִּלָּכֵ֑דוּ הִנֵּ֤ה בִדְבַר־ יְהוָה֙ מָאָ֔סוּ וְחָכְמַֽת־ מֶ֖ה לָהֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: Therefore I will give their wives to other men and their fields to new owners. For from the least of them to the greatest, all are greedy for gain; from prophet to priest, all practice deceit.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Judah.
God says he will punish them.
God will give their wives to other men.
God will give their fields to new owners.
All the people are greedy for gain.
This includes everyone, from the least to the greatest.
The prophets are greedy.
The priests are greedy.
All of them practice deceit.
No one is honest.
Everyone seeks their own advantage.
passages.original: לָכֵן֩ אֶתֵּ֨ן אֶת־ נְשֵׁיהֶ֜ם לַאֲחֵרִ֗ים שְׂדֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ לְי֣וֹרְשִׁ֔ים כִּ֤י מִקָּטֹן֙ וְעַד־ גָּד֔וֹל כֻּלֹּ֖ה בֹּצֵ֣עַ בָּ֑צַע מִנָּבִיא֙ וְעַד־ כֹּהֵ֔ן כֻּלֹּ֖ה עֹ֥שֶׂה שָּֽׁקֶר׃

passages.text: They dress the wound of the daughter of My people with very little care, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there is no peace at all.
passages.sermon:
The leaders and teachers in Israel act carelessly.
They see that my people are hurt.
They try to heal the wound quickly and lightly.
They do not give real help.
They say, “Peace, peace.”
They promise safety and calm.
But there is no peace.
Their words are false.
The people still suffer.
The leaders do not fix the real problem.
passages.original: וַיְרַפּ֞וּ אֶת־ שֶׁ֤בֶר בַּת־ עַמִּי֙ עַל־ נְקַלָּ֔ה לֵאמֹ֖ר שָׁל֣וֹם׀ שָׁל֑וֹם וְאֵ֖ין שָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Are they ashamed of the abomination they have committed? No, they have no shame at all; they do not even know how to blush. So they will fall among the fallen; when I punish them, they will collapse, says the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about the people of Judah.
The people of Judah have committed abominations.
They should feel ashamed.
But they do not feel shame.
They do not even know how to blush.
They do not recognize their disgrace.
Therefore, they will fall with those who have already fallen.
When the LORD punishes them, they will stumble and collapse.
The LORD has declared this.
passages.original: הֹבִ֕שׁוּ כִּ֥י תוֹעֵבָ֖ה עָשׂ֑וּ גַּם־ בּ֣וֹשׁ לֹֽא־ יֵבֹ֗שׁוּ וְהִכָּלֵם֙ לֹ֣א יָדָ֔עוּ לָכֵ֞ן יִפְּל֣וּ בַנֹּפְלִ֗ים בְּעֵ֧ת פְּקֻדָּתָ֛ם יִכָּשְׁל֖וּ אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: I will take away their harvest, declares the LORD. There will be no grapes on the vine, nor figs on the tree, and even the leaf will wither. Whatever I have given them will be lost to them.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD says, "I will gather them and take them away."
There are no grapes on the vine.
There are no figs on the fig tree.
The leaf has withered.
Everything I gave them will pass away from them."
passages.original: אָסֹ֥ף אֲסִיפֵ֖ם נְאֻם־ יְהֹוָ֑ה אֵין֩ עֲנָבִ֨ים בַּגֶּ֜פֶן וְאֵ֧ין תְּאֵנִ֣ים בַּתְּאֵנָ֗ה וְהֶֽעָלֶה֙ נָבֵ֔ל וָאֶתֵּ֥ן לָהֶ֖ם יַעַבְרֽוּם׃

passages.text: Why are we just sitting here? Gather together, let us flee to the fortified cities and perish there, for the LORD our God has doomed us. He has given us poisoned water to drink, because we have sinned against the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The people of Judah have sinned against the LORD their God.
They sit in despair.
They ask, “Why are we just sitting here?”
They say, “Let us gather together.”
They say, “Let us go to the fortified cities.”
They say, “Let us die there.”
The LORD our God has doomed us.
He has given us poisoned water to drink.
We have sinned against the LORD.
passages.original: עַל־ מָה֙ אֲנַ֣חְנוּ יֹֽשְׁבִ֔ים הֵֽאָסְפ֗וּ וְנָב֛וֹא אֶל־ עָרֵ֥י הַמִּבְצָ֖ר וְנִדְּמָה־ שָּׁ֑ם כִּי֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֵ֤ינוּ הֲדִמָּ֙נוּ֙ וַיַּשְׁקֵ֣נוּ מֵי־ רֹ֔אשׁ כִּ֥י חָטָ֖אנוּ לַיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: We hoped for peace, but no good has come, for a time of healing, but there was only terror.
passages.sermon:
The people hoped for peace.
No good came.
They waited for a time of healing.
They found only terror.
passages.original: קַוֵּ֥ה לְשָׁל֖וֹם וְאֵ֣ין ט֑וֹב לְעֵ֥ת מַרְפֵּ֖ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה בְעָתָֽה׃

passages.text: The snorting of enemy horses is heard from Dan. At the sound of the neighing of mighty steeds, the whole land quakes. They come to devour the land and everything in it, the city and all who dwell in it.
passages.sermon:
Enemy horses snort loudly.
People hear this sound from Dan.
Mighty horses neigh.
Their neighing shakes the whole land.
The enemy comes.
They devour the land.
They consume everything in the land.
They destroy the city.
They harm all who live in the city.
passages.original: מִדָּ֤ן נִשְׁמַע֙ נַחְרַ֣ת סוּסָ֗יו מִקּוֹל֙ מִצְהֲל֣וֹת אַבִּירָ֔יו רָעֲשָׁ֖ה כָּל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיָּב֗וֹאוּ וַיֹּֽאכְלוּ֙ אֶ֣רֶץ וּמְלוֹאָ֔הּ עִ֖יר וְיֹ֥שְׁבֵי בָֽהּ׃ס

passages.text: “For behold, I will send snakes among you, vipers that cannot be charmed, and they will bite you,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to His people.
The LORD says, "I will send snakes among you."
These snakes are vipers.
No one can charm these vipers.
These vipers will bite you."
The LORD Himself declares this.
passages.original: כִּי֩ הִנְנִ֨י מְשַׁלֵּ֜חַ בָּכֶ֗ם נְחָשִׁים֙ צִפְעֹנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵין־ לָהֶ֖ם לָ֑חַשׁ וְנִשְּׁכ֥וּ אֶתְכֶ֖ם נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: My sorrow is beyond healing; my heart is faint within me.
passages.sermon: I feel deep sorrow.\r\nMy sorrow is too great to heal.\r\nMy heart feels weak inside me.
passages.original: מַבְלִ֥יגִיתִ֖י עֲלֵ֣י יָג֑וֹן עָלַ֖י לִבִּ֥י דַוָּֽי׃

passages.text: Listen to the cry of the daughter of my people from a land far away: “Is the LORD no longer in Zion? Is her King no longer there?” “Why have they provoked Me to anger with their carved images, with their worthless foreign idols?”
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel are suffering.
They are far from their homeland.
They cry out in distress.
They ask, “Is the LORD no longer in Zion?”
They ask, “Is her King no longer there?”
The LORD answers.
He says, “Why have they made Me angry?”
He says, “They have worshiped carved images.”
He says, “They have trusted worthless foreign idols.”
passages.original: הִנֵּה־ ק֞וֹל שַֽׁוְעַ֣ת בַּת־ עַמִּ֗י מֵאֶ֙רֶץ֙ מַרְחַקִּ֔ים הַֽיהוָה֙ אֵ֣ין בְּצִיּ֔וֹן אִם־ מַלְכָּ֖הּ אֵ֣ין בָּ֑הּ מַדּ֗וּעַ הִכְעִס֛וּנִי בִּפְסִלֵיהֶ֖ם בְּהַבְלֵ֥י נֵכָֽר׃

passages.text: “The harvest has passed, the summer has ended, but we have not been saved.”
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel speak.
They say the harvest has passed.
They say the summer has ended.
They say we have not been saved.
passages.original: עָבַ֥ר קָצִ֖יר כָּ֣לָה קָ֑יִץ וַאֲנַ֖חְנוּ ל֥וֹא נוֹשָֽׁעְנוּ׃

passages.text: For the brokenness of the daughter of my people I am crushed. I mourn; horror has gripped me.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah is a prophet of God.
He speaks about the suffering of his people.
The people of Israel are broken.
Their pain crushes Jeremiah.
He feels deep sorrow.
He mourns for them.
Horror holds him tightly.
passages.original: עַל־ שֶׁ֥בֶר בַּת־ עַמִּ֖י הָשְׁבָּ֑רְתִּי קָדַ֕רְתִּי שַׁמָּ֖ה הֶחֱזִקָֽתְנִי׃

passages.text: Is there no balm in Gilead? Is no physician there? Why then has the health of the daughter of my people not been restored?
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah is a prophet of God.
He speaks about the suffering of his people.
He asks a question.
He says, “Is there no balm in Gilead?”
He asks, “Is there no physician there?”
He wonders why healing has not come.
He says, “Why then has the health of the daughter of my people not been restored?”
passages.original: הַצֳרִי֙ אֵ֣ין בְּגִלְעָ֔ד אִם־ רֹפֵ֖א אֵ֣ין שָׁ֑ם כִּ֗י מַדּ֙וּעַ֙ לֹ֣א עָֽלְתָ֔ה אֲרֻכַ֖ת בַּת־ עַמִּֽי׃
